result.summary: The environment is a wide, multi-lane arterial road with narrow sidewalks and no visible pedestrian crossings or traffic calming measures. High vehicle speeds are likely due to the road width and lack of physical interventions, creating a hostile environment for pedestrians. While sidewalks are present, they lack adequate buffers from traffic, especially on the commercial side of the street.

hazards.name: Wide Roadway and High Speed Design
hazards.description: The multi-lane configuration and wide asphalt surface encourage high vehicle speeds and create a long, unprotected crossing distance for pedestrians.
hazards.location_in_image: Center roadway extending into the distance

hazards.name: Lack of Pedestrian Crossings
hazards.description: There are no marked crosswalks or pedestrian signals visible, forcing pedestrians to cross multiple lanes of traffic without protection.

hazards.name: Sidewalk Obstructions
hazards.description: Utility poles are located directly in the narrow sidewalk path on the right, reducing the effective walking width.

interventions.title: Road Diet
interventions.description: Reduce the number of travel lanes or lane widths to slow traffic and repurpose space for wider sidewalks or bike lanes.

interventions.title: Midblock Pedestrian Refuge Island
interventions.description: Install a raised median island to allow pedestrians to cross one direction of traffic at a time.

interventions.title: Curb Extensions
interventions.description: Extend the sidewalk into the parking lane at potential crossing points to increase pedestrian visibility and shorten crossing distances.

result.summary: The image depicts a residential street with row houses and a continuous, unobstructed sidewalk. The environment lacks pedestrian safety enhancements such as street trees, buffers, or traffic calming measures, and the roadway shows signs of pavement wear.

hazards.name: Lack of Pedestrian Buffer
hazards.description: The sidewalk is directly adjacent to the parking lane and roadway with no physical separation like trees or bollards.
hazards.location_in_image: Along the curb line in front of the row houses.

hazards.name: Poor Roadway Pavement
hazards.description: Visible cracking and patching in the asphalt surface can create uneven footing for pedestrians crossing the street.

interventions.title: Street Trees and Greenery
interventions.description: Install street trees to provide a physical and psychological buffer between the sidewalk and the street.

interventions.title: Curb Extensions
interventions.description: Add curb extensions to shorten crossing distances and improve visibility between pedestrians and drivers.

result.summary: The environment is a wide urban arterial with multiple travel lanes and a significant crossing distance for pedestrians. While sidewalks are present on both sides, they lack substantial buffers from moving traffic, and the absence of a median refuge increases exposure risk during crossings.

hazards.name: Long Crossing Distance
hazards.description: The wide roadway requires pedestrians to cross multiple lanes of traffic without a refuge, increasing exposure time.
hazards.location_in_image: Center foreground across the main roadway

hazards.name: Visual Obstructions
hazards.description: Utility poles and parked vehicles near the intersection may block sightlines between drivers and pedestrians.
hazards.location_in_image: Left side of the street near the sidewalk edge

interventions.title: Pedestrian Refuge Island
interventions.description: Install a raised median island to allow pedestrians to cross one direction of traffic at a time.

interventions.title: Curb Extensions
interventions.description: Construct bulb-outs at the intersection to shorten the crossing distance and improve visibility.

interventions.title: Street Trees and Buffers
interventions.description: Add a planting strip or street trees to provide a physical and psychological buffer between the sidewalk and the roadway.

result.summary: The image shows a midblock pedestrian crossing on a multi-lane roadway with some safety enhancements like flexible bollards and a marked crosswalk. However, the crossing distance is significant across four lanes of traffic without a raised refuge island or signalized control.

hazards.name: Long Crossing Distance
hazards.description: Pedestrians must cross four lanes of traffic without a central refuge island, increasing exposure time to vehicles.
hazards.location_in_image: Center of the roadway at the marked crosswalk

hazards.name: Visual Obstruction from Parked Cars
hazards.description: Parked vehicles on the far side of the street may block the sightlines between drivers and pedestrians entering the crosswalk.
hazards.location_in_image: Far side curb line adjacent to the crosswalk

interventions.title: Pedestrian Refuge Island
interventions.description: Install a raised median island at the center of the crosswalk to allow pedestrians to cross one direction of traffic at a time.

interventions.title: Rectangular Rapid Flashing Beacon (RRFB)
interventions.description: Add user-actuated amber LEDs to the crossing signs to increase driver yielding rates at this midblock location.

interventions.title: Daylighting
interventions.description: Remove parking spaces immediately adjacent to the crosswalk to improve visibility for both pedestrians and drivers.
